artifacts.summary: Closes Site 3 of the three documented Containment-predicate sites: git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 resolution block now strips every deployed-tree file_scope entry exactly as git-commit-phase.sh's Site-2 Self-Check already does, pinned by a new Z19 case and Case 26's restored end-to-end assertion, with git-staging-scope.md updated to record the closure.

completion_data.completion_summary: Ported git-commit-phase.sh's Site-2 deployed-tree file_scope strip into git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 resolution block (Site 3), closing the gap where a .claude-prefixed file_scope entry admitted at Site 2 was still independently vetoed at Site 3. Added regression case Z19, restored test-git-commit-phase.sh's Case 26 to its full end-to-end assertion, confirmed Case 20 unaffected, and updated git-staging-scope.md to record that only the read-only proposed_file_scope_lookup annotation remains site-2-only.

memory_candidates.content: When porting an identical mechanism between two documented chokepoints of the same predicate (e.g. git-commit-phase.sh's Site-2 Containment Self-Check and git-commit-scoped.sh's Site-3 V10 resolution), check each site's own local conventions before copying verbatim: one site may define a warn() helper while the sibling site has no such helper and uses inline `echo "WARN: ..." >&2` instead, and loop variable names used at one site (e.g. `entry`) may already be in use by an unrelated function at the other site, requiring distinct names to avoid shadowing/collision.

To sanity-check that a new regression case genuinely pins the behaviour it claims to (rather than passing for an incidental reason), temporarily revert the fix in the working copy only (never committed), re-run the suite, and confirm the new case specifically fails with the expected error shape -- then restore the fix and verify `git diff` against HEAD is empty before proceeding. This is cheap and catches a case that would pass regardless of the fix.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh V10 Containment resolution
sapience_notes.value: The V10 effective-scope resolution block in git-commit-scoped.sh now strips every deployed-tree (.claude/.claude//.claude/*) file_scope entry immediately after the raw containment_scope_arr population loop and before the non-emptiness guard, mirroring git-commit-phase.sh's own Site-2 Containment Self-Check. A file_scope consisting solely of deployed-tree entries now fails open (disables the V10 check entirely) at both sites, not just one.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh warning convention
sapience_notes.value: git-commit-scoped.sh defines no warn() helper function; every V9/V10/V13 warning in that script is an inline `echo "WARN: git-commit-scoped.sh: ..." >&2` call. This differs from git-commit-phase.sh, which does define a warn() helper. Porting a warning call between the two scripts requires translating the convention, not copying verbatim.

sapience_notes.subject: test-git-commit-scoped.sh Z-series fixture helper
sapience_notes.value: build_repo_with_scope(task_number, project_name, file_scope_json) in test-git-commit-scoped.sh seeds specs/999_probe/a.txt, specs/999_probe/b.txt (both inside the implicit task-directory scope member, so neither can ever be the dropped path in a partial-drop case), and specs/998_sibling/out.txt under a genuinely separate sibling task directory specifically so callers have an out-of-scope candidate path available without extra setup.

sapience_notes.subject: proposed_file_scope_lookup asymmetry between Containment sites
sapience_notes.value: After closing the deployed-tree strip asymmetry between git-commit-phase.sh (Site 2) and git-commit-scoped.sh (Site 3), exactly one deliberate asymmetry remains between the two sites: Site 2's read-only proposed_file_scope_lookup, which only annotates a repeat drop's warning text and never affects the admit/reject decision. It stays unmirrored at Site 3 because Site 3 has no equivalent drop-warning-annotation surface to mirror it onto -- not an oversight, a structural absence.

sapience_notes.subject: Admitting-union design for proposed_file_scope was tried and rejected
sapience_notes.value: An earlier design that would union proposed_file_scope into containment_scope_arr (so a path proposed by Site 2 would be admitted by Site 3 too) was built and rejected: it regressed test-git-commit-phase.sh's own idempotence fixture (Case 20), because Site 3 independently vetoes a path Site 2 admits only on the strength of a not-yet-merged deposit, making Site 2 either falsely report success or hard-fail on a path that genuinely never lands. The deployed-tree strip ported in this task is a narrower, independently-safe fix that does not reintroduce this rejected design.
